name: GridDB
tagline: Toshiba's memory-first container database for IoT time series, with per-container ACID and SQL.
description: GridDB is a distributed database from Toshiba Digital Solutions aimed at industrial IoT and social-infrastructure systems. Data is organised into containers, either time-series or general collections keyed by row, kept memory-first with disk persistence, and spread across a cluster that promotes a new master automatically when nodes fail. It offers a NoSQL API with ACID guarantees inside each container plus a SQL interface, which the community edition has included since version 5. Toshiba runs it in energy, manufacturing and transport projects and offers GridDB Cloud as a managed service. The server is AGPL-3.0 with Apache-licensed clients, and adoption outside Japan is modest.

pricing.notes: Community edition is free; GridDB Enterprise is licensed by Toshiba; GridDB Cloud is a subscription service.

scale.notes: Containers are partitioned and replicated across nodes; capacity grows by adding nodes.

strengths: Memory-first design gives low-latency reads and writes on sensor data
ACID transactions within a container, unusual for a TSDB
Time-series containers with expiry and built-in sampling functions
Backed by Toshiba with long-running industrial deployments
weaknesses: Small community and ecosystem outside Japan
SQL coverage and tooling lag mainstream SQL databases
useCases: IoT apps needing per-device transactional updates
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a broad third-party ecosystem
